title: HubSpot private app access token as a Bearer header value or the tokenKey body member
summary: A synthetic opaque value after the Bearer scheme in a raw request and a quoted curl -H argument, and as the tokenKey member of the JSON body of an access-token-info request in a raw request and a curl --data argument.
rationale: HubSpot documents the private app access token as the value of the Authorization header after Bearer, and as the tokenKey body field of POST /oauth/v2/private-apps/get/access-token-info (contract claims private-app-token-exists and token-carried-in-info-request-body). HubSpot states no prefix, alphabet, length or grouping (no-hubspot-statement-of-token-layout), so the value is flagged because of where it sits, not its shape; the pat-na1- and UUID-shaped leads are not used. The extent is the value only. The Bearer slot is shared with OAuth access tokens and Service Keys, which an existing Case covers (hubspot-bearer-authorization-header-value); this Case names the private app family and adds the tokenKey member. Existing legacy private apps continue to work while creation of new ones is being disabled (legacy-creation-disabled-schedule).

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, redact-secret#1228 Group C). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: a value in an Authorization: Bearer header or the tokenKey member of an access-token-info request to HubSpot is treated as a credential whatever its shape. HubSpot documents the Bearer header and the tokenKey body field (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic attribution are the project's decisions. No subtype is inferred, and no prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: When making a call to one of the HubSpot API endpoints, set the value of the Authorization field to Bearer [YOUR_TOKEN].
